threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You say 'please' and 'thank you' to the bus drivers. You'll stop once you realize they don't even look up.
Last night on the 77, a guy serenaded the whole bus with a ukulele version of Spice Girls. Almost made the 30-minute wait for a bus home worth it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Sitting in the park, I overheard kids arguing over who gets to be a pigeon today. That’s when I realized this place is a blend of chaos and charm.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find currywurst served up with a side of techno beats from the street, blending fast food and nightlife like nowhere else.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by how they roll their eyes when someone tries to make eye contact on a crowded Muni bus.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 at Civic Center, and a whole yoga class decided to stretch in the aisle. Only in SF would that be a normal bus ride.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' is just Gaudí and parks, but the real vibe’s in our local bars, where the same faces gather every night for a quiet drink.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot a newbie by the way they take a picture of every menu item at local bars—definitely a dead giveaway!

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' when you mean the 'L' train; only locals know the true grit of the rails here.
Saw a guy in a bright orange onesie serenading the bus driver on the 68. Only in Brixton at 2 AM, I swear.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: One rainy afternoon, I saw an old man feeding pigeons outside the Körnerpark while a group of kids danced in the puddles—classic Neukölln moment.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find a bar that serves cocktails in mason jars, while the jukebox plays vinyl records from local bands no one outside Berlin knows.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they know to avoid Civic Center station at rush hour now—it's a hot mess with train delays and smoke from that BART scare.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, watched a guy pull out a sax during a 38 Geary wait, effortlessly blending notes with the screech of the bus brakes. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the bars close early, but in Gràcia, some don’t even get going until after 1 AM. The real night just starts then.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their awkward attempts at Catalan, especially when they mix up 'bon dia' and 'bona tarda'.
